## LLM Recipe

### 1.1 Data Curation &amp; Tokenization

#### [MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12659>)

MagicBeanStalk decomposes hard problems into verified subproblems, then recombines new variants into training tasks calibrated to a target model and response budget. It turns otherwise uninformative all-failure reward groups into useful reinforcement-learning data while preserving the reasoning skills that made the original seeds valuable.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T04:36:31.851Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Synthetic Data, RLVR, Difficulty Calibration

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12659>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Delayed discovery of the October 12 new-submission batch; availability is inferred from that dated primary-category batch and the official schedule. Sections 2–4 and Appendices D–G provide synthesis controls, qualification screens and evaluations; gpt-oss-120b improves from 61.2 to 69.8 average pass@1 across eight math benchmarks at 16K output tokens.

**Limitations:** Difficulty is a finite-sample, policy-and-budget-dependent estimate. Synthesis and some verification rely on proprietary teachers; data release is promised upon acceptance. Extra synthesis cost is not an end-to-end efficiency win. Synthetic errors and unequal sample counts limit cross-model comparisons; no results were independently reproduced.

### 1.2 Model Architecture &amp; Scaling Laws

#### [Overcoming Data Imbalances with Expert Selection Biases](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13370>)

COAX adds category-dependent biases to expert selection during pretraining, giving scarce languages or modalities a larger preferred expert pool while keeping the number of active experts per token fixed. This supplies a simple capacity-allocation control for imbalanced training mixtures, with most multilingual and multimodal loss gains retained after removing the bias for standard inference.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T04:36:31.851Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Mixture of Experts, Multilingual Training, Capacity Allocation

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13370>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Delayed discovery of the October 12 new-submission batch, with availability inferred using the official schedule. Sections 3–6 and Appendices B, F and G compare matched MoEs up to 10.6B total parameters, routing alternatives and data upsampling; seven-minority-language validation loss improves 0.286% relative in the largest eight-language setup.

**Limitations:** Most evidence concerns held-out next-token loss; multilingual task benchmarks are inconclusive and free generation remains undertrained. Some domains regress without inference-time bias. Training overhead ranges from about 20% at the smallest scale to 1.3%–2.4% in tested large/coarse configurations; no public implementation was verified.

### 1.9 Test-Time Scaling &amp; Inference Algorithms

#### [A Critical Look at Power Sampling when Test Time Sharpening LLMs](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13653>)

This study tests whether power-distribution sampling improves reasoning because it faithfully sharpens a model or simply searches for likely responses, and introduces a fine-tuning control that targets that distribution more directly. Its model-dependent results motivate testing inexpensive likelihood-based selection and low-temperature decoding before investing in more elaborate samplers.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T04:36:31.851Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Test-Time Scaling, Power Sampling, Controlled Evaluation

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/stat.ML/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13653>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Delayed discovery of the October 12 new-submission batch, with inferred availability grounded in the official schedule. Sections 3–5 and Table 1 compare three models on MATH500 and GPQA Diamond; simple selection often matches Power-SMC, while more faithful POWER-RLOO produces both gains and a length-collapse failure.

**Limitations:** Experiments use a 1,564-token generation cap, three models, two tasks and seed 0; results are not a universal rejection of sharpening. Training and inference costs are different. Code is promised upon acceptance; a broad prose claim about beating POWER-RLOO contradicts the Qwen-Instruct GPQA table, so it is not repeated.

### 1.10 Model Evaluation, Safety &amp; Interpretability

#### [Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks](<https://www.anthropic.com/research/distillation-defenses>)

Anthropic describes a layered defense against unauthorized reasoning extraction that combines protected-context boundaries, extraction classifiers and account-level abuse controls. Its new technical report connects information exposure to downstream distillation performance and documents deployment tradeoffs, offering a concrete case study for platforms that expose powerful reasoning models.

**Published:** 2026-10-12 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T04:37:12.000Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Model Extraction, Reasoning Distillation, Platform Safeguards

[Blog](<https://www.anthropic.com/research/distillation-defenses>)

**Evidence:** engineering-report; full-text. The October 12 report gives SWE-bench Verified scores of 80.4% versus 71.8% for a pretrained Claude student distilled from full versus summarized Opus 4.8 transcripts, and estimates 10-100x less reasoning-token extraction on its platform after classifier introduction. Delayed discovery concerns this report; its controls were introduced earlier.

**Limitations:** Internal author measurements lack released data, complete training controls and independent replication. The reported false-positive rate below 0.1% and platform-specific extraction estimates are not universal guarantees; highly persistent attacks remain untested. Legitimate integrations can require changes and benign blocked requests can incur charges. No code release was verified.

## AI Agent Dev

### 2.2 Tool Use &amp; Environment Interaction

#### [Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13416>)

Web$hell compiles webpages into addressable information and action objects, letting agents search stored evidence and operate live controls through one interface. This makes complex web tasks easier to continue across many pages; the authors report stronger results on six search, navigation and research benchmarks with comparable or lower model cost than their tested interfaces.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T04:39:34.000Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Web Interfaces, Persistent Evidence, Browser Actions

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13416>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Delayed discovery from the October 12 arXiv batch, absent the baseline and all 158 registry works; submission was October 9 at 11:23:40 UTC. Sections 3–6 and Appendices A–D expose deterministic compilation, persistent read-only prior states, controlled interface comparisons and association ablations. With GPT-5.6-Luna/high, Table 3 reports WebArena-Verified success 67.9% versus 57.8% for the combined search/browser/filesystem baseline.

**Limitations:** Work in progress using one principal model and finite benchmark subsets. Cost is model inference rather than total system cost: compilation adds 0.46–2.79 seconds per acquired page, and cached-token pricing affects comparisons. Stored page states cannot restore live browser state; no available implementation was verified and results were not independently reproduced.

### 2.8 Agent Evaluation &amp; Security

#### [AgentSWE: Can Coding Agents Build the Agent You Actually Want?](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13361>)

AgentSWE tests whether coding agents can create, edit and optimize the agents users request, freezing each delivery before running it on held-out cases derived from the requirements. Its 25 commissions expose a gap between convincing development demonstrations and working delivered behavior, giving builders a concrete evaluation for overfitting, incomplete runtimes and unsupported completion claims.

## AI Training &amp; Inference Infra

### 3.4 Attention, KV Cache &amp; Memory Systems

#### [Ember: Making Unified Virtual Memory Practical for Discrete-Memory GPUs](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13408>)

Ember keeps oversubscribed GPU allocations accessible in host memory and selectively promotes useful regions into GPU memory, with an adaptive variant using hardware access counters and proactive reclamation. This reduces page-migration thrashing when model weights exceed device capacity, offering a concrete memory-management design for constrained LLM inference rather than requiring the whole model to fit on the GPU.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T04:38:15.060Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Unified Memory, GPU Offloading, Memory Oversubscription

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.OS/recent>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13408>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Delayed discovery of the October 12 batch; October 9 v1 date retained, with public availability inferred from the dated listing and official schedule. Sections 4–8 distinguish stock-CUDA static placement from the patched-driver adaptive policy. Section 7.4 tests Qwen2.5-14B/Qwen3-32B generation on RTX 5080, A40 and H200, each capped to 16 GB; at 1.41x oversubscription, the static variant reports 4.7–13x over stock UVM.

**Limitations:** These are 128-token decode benchmarks, not serving throughput: no strategy exceeds 3 tokens/s in the oversubscribed cases. Adaptive placement requires a driver patch and administrator access; only managed allocations and one GPU-to-host tier are controlled. No dedicated source-code release was verified; the abstract's larger headline is not substituted for the narrower Section 7.4 result.

#### [SlackSwap: Bandwidth-Aware Activation Swapping and Recomputation for Memory-Efficient DNN Training](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13003>)

SlackSwap treats host-link time as a limited budget, offloading activations that would be expensive to rebuild and recomputing cheaper tensors once that transfer budget is exhausted. Its trace-driven simulations suggest that combining bandwidth-aware placement with asynchronous copies can retain training throughput under tight activation-memory budgets, while leaving real-system performance to be demonstrated.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T04:36:42.817Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Activation Memory, Offloading, Recomputation

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.DC/recent?skip=50&show=100>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13003>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Delayed discovery of the verified October 12 batch; original October 9 submission retained and availability inferred from the dated listing plus schedule. Algorithm 1 and Sections 3–4 specify two-pass planning, FIFO offloads and earliest-deadline-first prefetches. A100 simulations of BERT-Large, GPT-2 XL and a Llama-7B-style model retain 96.3–99.6% of unlimited-memory throughput at half the activation budget, 1.10–1.11x the best simulated baseline.

**Limitations:** All performance results are simulated. The model omits allocator fragmentation, copy-induced HBM contention, and shared PCIe/host-memory contention; model states remain resident on one GPU. The SwapAdvisor comparison omits its operator-order and memory-pool genetic search. No dedicated implementation or independent reproduction was verified.
